analysis:
Only base-side text of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 956-1467) was supplied, plus a truncated patch excerpt. The change is documentation only, with no source or control code. The visible patch excerpt shows a date bump (line 3), a new Swift-only optional `detail` field on autopilot status (head 854), and a new Swift-only optional `hold_seconds` on the `model_autopilot` command (head 1208). The patch is cut off, and the head ranges 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 are not visible. I could not review the head-side content of those ranges.

The base text covers prefix-cache v2 receipts, inference_request fields, the model_autopilot command and control messages, and App Attest protocol 3. This text relates to T-041 (prefix cache), TB-002, TB-011 and T-053. The visible additions do not weaken those controls. The `hold_seconds` field is documented as a bounded value (0...86400). It is placement-only and is rejected as `invalid_command` without `load_model_id`. It stays inside the existing model_autopilot session/revision/expiry gating, and the docs say shadow leases cannot authorize the message. The `detail` field is a diagnostic string, sent with consent only, and carries a busy reason. It is not described as an authorization or capacity signal. The base-side text keeps the explicit statements that a stale routing hint never grants a cache hit and that the status frame cannot change capacity.

Open questions for integration: (1) the unseen remainder of the patch, including the truncated `hold_seconds` row and the head ranges 1355-1380 and 1470-1472; (2) whether the Swift-only `hold_seconds` and `detail` fields are enforced by provider code that is not supplied here, such as bounds validation and the persistence of holds across commands. I found no concrete regression, but coverage is incomplete.
